Antibiotics were prescribed unnecessarily in 42.2% of encounters for indicated conditions.

operand_cells.value: Resident physicians had a lower rate of inappropriate prescriptions than attending physicians and advanced practice providers. Attending physicians issued 65.3% of all FQ prescriptions, with cystitis/pyelonephritis being the most common indication.

The Antibiotic Likelihood Index (ALI) which measures the proportion of encounters with an antibiotic prescription within six reason for visit categories accounting for over 80% of all antibiotic prescriptions in primary care pediatric practice can serve as a quality metric for antimicrobial stewardship in primary care.
